n5fdc6655acc1: BackgroundAmbient artificial intelligence (AI) medical scribes may reduce documentation burden and clinician burnout. A secondary 3-group ITS compared enrolled nonusers, low users, and high users.Setting14-hospital health system in Boston, Massachusetts.Participants902 outpatient clinicians enrolled in Heidi; 605 users and 297 enrolled nonusers.InterventionHeidi enrollment after system-wide implementation beginning January 2025.MeasurementsThe primary outcome was note-active time. Secondary outcomes included same-day and after-hours note closures, note length, and work relative value units (wRVUs).Results1 637 227 encounters had notes authored by enrolled clinicians between 1 July 2024 and 31 January 2026. Enrollment was associated with an immediate reduction in note-active time (-1.21 minutes [95% CI, -1.74 to -0.68 minutes]), with larger reductions among high users (-2.50 minutes [CI, -3.55 to -1.45 minutes]) than nonusers (difference, -2.20 minutes [CI, -3.46 to -0.95 minutes]) and low users (difference, -1.72 minutes [CI, -3.03 to -0.40 minutes]). High users had greater increases in note length than nonusers (difference, +170.90 characters [CI, 21.07 to 320.70 characters]) and low users (difference, +270.70 characters [CI, 131.04 to 410.36 characters]). n939d3be5d6f9: BackgroundRandomized clinical trials (RCTs) have compared laparoscopic liver resection (LLR) and open liver resection (OLR) for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM); however, long-term outcomes and subgroup effects have not been comprehensively evaluated.PurposeTo compare postoperative and long-term oncologic outcomes after LLR versus OLR for CRLM using individual participant data from RCTs.Data sourcesPubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception through March 2025 for RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.Study selectionEligible studies were RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.Data extractionIndividual participant data, including unpublished data, were obtained from trial investigators of all 4 published RCTs.Data synthesisAnalyses used a modified intention-to-treat approach and 1-stage individual participant data meta-analysis (IPDMA) with trial-adjusted regression models and g-computation to estimate standardized treatment effects across outcomes, with 95% CIs obtained by nonparametric bootstrap resampling. n614e43669602: To the Editor The Viewpoint article by Drs Singh and Mello provides a balanced discussion of advertising in artificial intelligence (AI)–powered clinical decision support (CDS). It is worth highlighting that the authors state that AI-powered CDS often is free. Did we not say the same about drug company–sponsored lunches and so-called “free” pens and other giveaways in the 1990s? Some will recall when drug companies sponsored lunches for faculty and trainees, gave away pens and other branded items, and sometimes accompanied physicians on rounds. For those who trained more recently, please know that this practice was widely accepted; however, we eventually learned that there is, in fact, no free lunch. Now, we must learn there is no free CDS. Singh and Mello note that while “some products operate on a subscription model, others such as OpenEvidence use advertising revenue to offer access without charge.” It is surprising and disappointing that clinicians may think they are receiving CDS for free. Perhaps they have forgotten—or may have never learned—that drug company advertisements influence prescribing behavior when they appear alongside information intended to educate physicians and support clinical practice. Clearly the drug companies themselves have not forgotten. Twenty years ago, the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations revised its code of ethics and barred gifts or money that could influence prescribing behavior. CDS companies that embed pharmaceutical advertisements in their products should end this practice and, if they do not, the pharmaceutical industry should do so. Better yet, clinicians should recognize they have other options without industry advertisements and should choose such CDS tools.
ndd27c90df34d: In Reply We appreciate the thoughtful letters in response to our Viewpoint. We agree with Dr Ziegelstein that the simplest solution to the ethical quandaries of advertising in AI-powered CDS tools would be for the AI-powered CDS companies that use advertisements and/or the pharmaceutical companies that partner with them to end this practice altogether. However, this is unlikely to happen, given that advertising is a potentially more lucrative revenue source than other options such as subscriptions. Ziegelstein’s suggestion that clinicians recognize they have other options and choose CDS tools that do not embed advertisements seems more realistic, particularly if their organizational employers nudge them in this direction. Historically, once Epocrates (a free drug information app) began supporting ads at the point of care, its credibility with its physician users eroded and other services such as UpToDate ultimately won out.

n1bce3d09872e: “Do I need to treat this blood pressure?” is one of the most common questions to pass through the minds of acute care pediatricians during a typical day in the hospital. Blood pressure generally increases with somatic growth, reflecting developmental changes in stroke volume, vascular structure and function, and neurohumoral regulation. As a result of interindividual variation across the developmental stages of childhood, there is a wide range of acceptable blood pressure values. There is also long-standing ambiguity about what should be considered the limits of acceptable blood pressure, particularly among hospitalized children. Age-based reference values offer a starting point, although the threshold used to identify an unusually low blood pressure may differ from the pressure needed to maintain adequate organ perfusion. This uncertainty can create substantial tension when a clinician faces the decision whether to manage potentially low blood pressure in a child. Treatments for potentially low blood pressure can also vary widely, from temporary stimulation to administration of vasopressor and inotropic medications through a central vascular catheter. The clinical question of whether to manage low blood pressure is driven by concern that withholding treatment could cause harm that is hard to measure.

nb0a14d91757e: In Reply We thank Dr Huynh and colleagues for their thoughtful comments on our economic evaluation of HPSA-FIT co-testing. ned2ea9deb4f7: In “Holding Hope,” the poem’s crux is not simply the devastating neurologic sign of “fixed pupils,” but also the way this medical phrase is transformed in the ear of the shocked sibling of a mortally wounded patient into the impossible mercy of healing: “[t]hey fixed his pupils.” The clinical distancing inherent in a bedside case presentation, reflexively performed before a disbelieving family member, is translated by a kind of poetic mishearing from incomprehensible loss into hopeful repair. The patient’s sibling seems to only grasp fragments of reality, while the physicians only offer partial truths. Even the clinician-speaker of the poem struggles with what can be held medically vs emotionally, the gasping lines and broken-up stanzas structurally reflecting the patient’s wounded brain and body and the heartbreak of both family member and physician. Yet poetry here does not really restore hope like some kind of harmless magic bullet, nor does it heal the lethal real-world gunshot wounds; more painfully, perhaps, it tries to reconcile brutal finality with the disconsolate wish it were not so. Thus the poem ultimately becomes an “antipresentation” of sorts, in which medical facts are melded with human truths, words can have double meanings, and what can be held is both the obligatory, dire prognosis and its denial. The insistence on what poetry can hear, and what no case presentation could ever convey, is reiterated in the poem’s final lines, expressed in the importunate paradox of the patient’s sibling’s repeated words: “…you heard/‘They fixed his pupils.’”

n3601df796d51: To the Editor A recent Perspective proposed a federal licensure framework for autonomous clinical artificial intelligence (AI) modeled on physician credentialing. We disagree with the analogy. Medical licensure regulates a professional actor with fiduciary duties, moral agency, personal accountability, and the ability to refuse unsafe action. A software product has none of these. It is deployed by identifiable commercial and institutional actors. Granting it professional standing does not create accountability; it obscures it.
nc2292f178e8d: In Reply We thank the correspondents for their Letters to the Editor, which converge on 1 concern—that autonomous clinical AI is not a person—and we agree. Our proposal never attributes moral agency to software, and licensure does not require it. Drs Ferguson and Telemi and Dr Jiang argue that a product cannot be a practitioner. But we do not license software as a moral actor; we authorize a defined clinical function and attach accountability to identifiable human parties. Developers bear primary responsibility and deploying institutions secondary responsibility precisely because the model cannot. Licensure here is a mechanism for ongoing, outcome-based authorization, not a claim of personhood.

n97cd87ff8cdf: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women, contributes markedly to healthcare expenditures, and is projected to increase substantially by 2050 if current trends continue. There is growing recognition of the complex role of sex as a biologic variable and its influence on cardiovascular health and disease. However, cardiovascular risk remains underrecognized and underaddressed in girls and women, particularly as it relates to female-specific exposure to sex hormones (both endogenous and exogenous), which are systemic modulators of cardiovascular biology. Moreover, girls and women uniquely experience fragmented care spanning specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics and gynecology, maternal-fetal medicine, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Consequently, there is a need for a unified life course approach that addresses the female-specific interconnectedness of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health. To address these gaps, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, established a Female Life Stage framework to optimize the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women. Physiologic changes in sex hormones define clinically distinct life stages (ie, perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, postmenopause), which directly inform female-specific considerations for screening, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease. This presidential advisory details the framework and its scientific rationale, highlights opportunities for implementation across settings, and identifies priorities for research, clinician education, patient advocacy, and policy. This framework offers a transformative opportunity to equitably improve cardiovascular health for all girls and women.
n31ec66a5f292: Improving cardiovascular health in women is an urgent public health priority given the persistent and pervasive gaps in awareness, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease in this population. Advances in scientific understanding have led to increased recognition of female-specific considerations in cardiovascular disease, which informed the development of the Female Life Stage construct by the American Heart Association in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. This construct integrates assessment of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across life stages. However, gaps remain in operationalizing this construct and optimizing the delivery of patient-centered, interdisciplinary care among women. Over the past several decades, women’s cardiovascular centers have emerged as leaders, expanded rapidly, and elevated the recognition of cardiovascular diseases that exclusively, disproportionately, or differently affect women (eg, myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, Takotsubo syndrome). In this science advisory, we describe the current landscape of women’s cardiovascular centers and propose a national infrastructure to support the expansion of dedicated Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women’s Cardiovascular Care. These centers are conceptualized as interdisciplinary care models comprising 4 defining pillars: interdisciplinary clinical care, education and training, research, and community engagement. By establishing integrated pathways that span clinical disciplines, these centers can reduce fragmentation, enhance earlier risk identification, and expand opportunities to increase representation of women in clinical research. In doing so, they offer a bold opportunity for a scalable and equitable model to improve cardiovascular health for all women.
n1d56b4a88674: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages—perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)—to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.
n959e54935434: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.
n6b9c906fe7e4: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is classified by anatomic subtype: mitral atresia and aortic atresia (MA/AA), mitral stenosis and aortic atresia (MS/AA), and mitral stenosis and aortic stenosis (MS/AS). The MS/AA subtype is associated with ventriculocoronary connections (VCCs). We assessed whether specific HLHS subtypes are associated with an increased risk of mortality and whether this risk is stratified by VCCs identified during fetal or postnatal echocardiography. We also assessed whether the type of neonatal intervention performed modified the risk. We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of fetuses and infants <2 months old with HLHS who were admitted between January 2012 and December 2016 to participating Fetal Heart Society institutions. Clinical and demographic data were collected. Fetal and transthoracic echocardiograms from a subset of patients with MS/AA and those with suspected VCCs were reviewed. Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed, controlling for cardiac center (random effect), birth weight, genetic diagnosis, extracardiac malformation, and restricted/intact atrial septum. Among 16 centers, 591 patients were born alive with intention to treat. MA/AA was the most common subtype (261, 44%), followed by MS/AA (200, 34%) and MS/AS (130, 22%). Of those with MS/AA, 115 (58%) had suspected VCCs. Median follow-up was 9.0 (interquartile range: 7.0, 10.8) years. Overall transplant-free survival (TFS) was 55.6% at 5 years and 49.4% at 10 years. When comparing MA/AA, MS/AS, and MS/AA with and without VCCs (reference group: MS/AA without VCCs), MS/AA with VCCs had the lowest TFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.69 [1.12, 2.57]; 5-year TFS, 44.7%; 10-year TFS, 40.3%). This was followed by MA/AA (HR, 1.40 [0.95, 2.05]; 5-year TFS, 54.1%; 10-year TFS, 46.6%). Survival of MS/AA without VCCs (5-year TFS, 60.4%; 10-year TFS, 56.9%) was similar to MS/AS (HR, 0.91 [0.59, 1.41]; 5-year TFS, 65.0%; 10-year TFS, 58.3%). Among those with a prenatal diagnosis of HLHS (n=532), patients with MS/AA and VCCs suspected on fetal echocardiogram had a lower TFS compared with those with MS/AA without fetal suspicion for VCCs (HR, 1.79 [1.12, 2.85]). Fetal echocardiography was used to diagnose VCCs in 33 of 103 (32%) cases with MS/AA and VCCs suspected postnatally. n9a979e7a8a06: No therapies exist to reverse right ventricular failure (RVF), and the molecular mechanisms that drive RVF remain understudied. nbd649d566418: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, with 435 000 patients newly diagnosed worldwide each year. n1d78a20a6861: The treatment landscape of EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations has advanced remarkably over the past two decades. nbf23cba0be20: BackgroundNational cancer control plans (NCCPs) vary in scope and comprehensiveness, yet expert-led review is resource intensive and limits cross-country comparability. Financing showed the largest gaps-only five of eleven financing sub-elements had median scores of 1·0 or less.InterpretationOur analysis suggests that NCCP comprehensiveness varies substantially between countries with consistent weaknesses in financing, outcome measurement, and contextual analysis. A shared health systems framework and scalable AI appraisal tools, such as PRISM, could support more complete, comparable, and actionable plans to strengthen cancer control globally by providing the possibility for rapid analysis of comprehensiveness of NCCPs and generation of timely, achievable, and evidence-informed, context-specific plans that use the latest data.FundingHarvard University.
neb745a437649: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. n9b8e8ddc7353: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). This Policy Review details the importance, development, and anticipated impact of this new guideline. n499627ac072d: BackgroundAnti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. ne805cbc8e893: BackgroundDivarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.MethodsIn this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. nc84ddc78d69c: BackgroundSavolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). nf41e676512a9: BackgroundPembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.MethodsIn this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. n365a6c6e67cf: BackgroundTo our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). n13e34fe4211f: BackgroundThe combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. n44e6f9b772f2: BackgroundThe standard of care for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer continues to evolve. n226c2adf03c3: BackgroundEndovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. neade2a36331e: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. These findings help explain why immune-modifying therapies suppress relapses and new lesion formation. However, susceptibility genetics does not adequately explain disability accumulation, variation in disease course, or treatment response. Evidence from rare-variant studies, genetic studies of disease severity and disability progression, epigenetic analyses, gene-environment studies, and Epstein-Barr virus research is beginning to extend this genetic framework from susceptibility to disease expression. Still, the direct clinical relevance of this research remains constrained by modest individual-level predictive value, underpowered studies of genetic determinants of disease severity and disability progression, complex regulatory mechanisms linking variants to function, and restricted generalisability across populations. At present, multiple sclerosis genetics is most useful for interpreting mechanisms, prioritising therapeutic targets, supporting causal inference, informing biomarker discovery, and enriching research cohorts. Future clinical value will likely depend on integrating genetic architecture with longitudinal clinical, imaging, biomarker, and multi-omic data to identify the contexts in which prevention or treatment is most likely to succeed.

n1622f2febff5: Variants in the ion channel gene KCNQ1 are the leading cause of congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS), a disorder characterized by QT prolongation and risk of fatal arrhythmias. n306a63f493b3: Chagas disease (ChD), a neglected cardiovascular condition, affects 7.5 to 10.5 million people worldwide. nc72d96d4cb32: Radiation-associated coronary artery disease (RACAD) is a distinct form of coronary artery disease with several specific biological and clinical aspects as well as key knowledge gaps. RACAD is prevalent in patients with cardiac exposure to radiotherapy. As radiotherapy is integral to the effective treatment of many thoracic malignancies, improved long-term survivorship is coupled with increased risk for RACAD. Ionizing radiation induces free radical generation and activation of proinflammatory cascades, leading to endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis. Risks for RACAD are determined both by radiotherapy, including the radiation dose and the proximity of coronary arteries to the radiotherapy field, and by patient-specific factors, such as younger age, higher baseline cardiovascular risk, and concurrent cardiotoxic systemic therapies. Importantly, radiotherapy delivery is highly individualized on the basis of tumor location and treatment strategy, resulting in heterogeneous coronary exposure to radiation and patient-to-patient variability. Clinical presentation may occur early, within 1 to 2 years, especially in patients with higher cardiac radiation doses (eg, lung or esophageal cancer), or after a latency period of 5 to 20 years with lower cardiac dose radiation exposure (eg, left-sided breast cancer). Patients generally present with symptoms similar to conventional coronary artery disease. However, RACAD symptoms may be underrecognized in cancer survivors due to overlapping treatment-related fatigue, pulmonary disease, or competing oncologic symptoms. Diagnosis and management generally follow standard coronary artery disease guidelines while incorporating cancer-specific considerations, such as planned oncologic surgeries, bleeding risk, postradiotherapy complications such as atretic internal mammary arteries, and cardiotoxic effects of systemic cancer therapies. Primary prevention of RACAD is critical, emphasizing advances in precision radiotherapy, including delivery techniques with improved coronary dosimetry, and cardiac shielding. Key knowledge gaps include understanding long-term outcomes with contemporary 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy techniques, validated cancer-specific risk prediction models on the basis of coronary dosimetry, optimal surveillance protocols, targeted molecular pharmacotherapies, and risk analysis of percutaneous versus surgical management of RACAD. Prospective studies are needed to develop cancer- and dosimetry-specific risk calculators, validating cardioprotective interventions, and improving multidisciplinary cardio-oncology collaboration to optimize early detection of RACAD and timely intervention in the growing population of cancer survivors.

na5ee85f8664c: Attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a medical condition that is present in approximately 2.5% of adults worldwide and manifests in a variety of different ways across the lifespan. nc323dcc0f863: The discovery of antibody-mediated glial and neuronal disorders has transformed the diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases previously considered idiopathic or not recognised as immune-mediated. Antibody-mediated disorders targeting glial aquaporin-4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein are distinct nosological entities, defined by specific targets, mechanisms, syndromes, and therapeutic implications. By contrast, antibody-mediated disorders targeting neuronal antigens (ie, autoimmune encephalitides) are still frequently analysed collectively, with data from different disorders pooled as if they represent a single disease rather than distinct entities. Evidence from anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and anti-IgLON5 disease (used here as exemplars of autoimmune encephalitides) indicates that individual autoimmune encephalitides differ in demographics, triggers, mechanisms, clinical manifestations, post-acute trajectories, and treatment requirements. The broad, heterogeneous presentations of autoimmune encephalitides require coordinated multidisciplinary care within and beyond neurology, involving specialists in paediatrics, infectious diseases, epilepsy, movement disorders, sleep medicine, intensive care, cognitive rehabilitation, and other relevant disciplines. Such interdisciplinary collaboration facilitates the recognition of new diseases and elucidation of the causes of previously unclassified disorders. Improving patient care requires not only aetiological and mechanistic insight to enable development of targeted therapies but also strengthened cross-specialty expertise to optimise diagnosis and management.
n5729197f38e9: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) affect more than 220 million people worldwide and are associated with cardiometabolic, endocrine, neurological, and psychiatric sequelae for years to decades after an acute injury. TBI and SCI in adults should be reclassified as acute-onset multisystem chronic-risk conditions. Existing cardiovascular, endocrine, and psychiatric services do not capture neurotrauma-specific risks, including trauma-induced hypopituitarism, autonomic dysregulation, accelerated ageing, and cognitive-behavioural impairment, so neurotrauma care is best framed as a missing node in chronic neurological care. We propose a risk-stratified pathway of care navigation, multisystem screening, and telehealth; convergence with adjacent stroke, cardiometabolic, memory, psychiatric, pain, and epilepsy services; and the financing, workforce, and registry reforms needed to deliver measurable reductions in 5-year mortality, avoidable rehospitalisation, and long-term disability.

n31c3ec0fc2d5: BackgroundExisting data on malformations associated with benzodiazepine use in pregnancy are conflicting.ObjectiveTo assess the risk for major congenital malformations from first-trimester exposure to benzodiazepines.DesignPopulation-based U.S. cohort study.SettingMedicaid (2000-2018) and Merative MarketScan (2003-2020) databases.ParticipantsPregnant persons enrolled from 90 days before pregnancy to 30 days after delivery, and their live-born infants enrolled for 90 days after birth.MeasurementsExposure was defined as at least 1 fill of a benzodiazepine in the first trimester. The investigators estimated relative risks (RRs) comparing exposed versus unexposed pregnancies with propensity score fine stratification weights to control for confounders. An RR of 1.3 or higher was prespecified as clinically significant.ResultsIn total, 51 339 of 2 478 434 (2.1%) publicly insured and 27 779 of 1 750 721 (1.6%) commercially insured pregnancies had benzodiazepine exposure. The adjusted absolute risks for any malformation in exposed versus unexposed pregnancies were 4.0% versus 4.1% for Medicaid and 4.9% versus 4.8% for MarketScan. The pooled adjusted RR was 0.99 (95% CI, 0.96 to 1.03). Associations with organ-specific malformations were not consistently observed in sensitivity analyses, nor was a dose-response relationship observed. Analyses of different benzodiazepines yielded similar results. The risk for selected organ-specific malformations was increased in some analyses of coexposure to benzodiazepines and other psychoactive medications, but a consistent pattern did not emerge.LimitationsPotential nondifferential exposure and outcome misclassification; analyses restricted to malformations prevalent at birth.ConclusionNo substantial increase in the risk for malformations was consistently identified across data sources. Findings from coexposure analyses were inconsistent and warrant further study.Primary funding sourceNational Institute of Child Health and Human Development.
n66c0a4c06330: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85–1.44]; P =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96–1.30]; P =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93–1.13]; P =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03–1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27–2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. nac885fae1340: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions. In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions. During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0–42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P <0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm 2 , regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm 2 , regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%–13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07–1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05–1.38]). Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.
n3c8c2b6e998c: Inactivation of ANGPTL3 (angiopoietin-like protein 3; A3) is a proven therapeutic strategy for lowering plasma lipid levels independently of the low-density lipoprotein receptor, yet the optimal approach to inactivate A3 remains unclear. A3 is proteolytically cleaved and circulates as full-length, N-terminal, and C-terminal fragments. The specific contribution of each form of A3, and of its paralog, ANGPTL8 (angiopoietin-like protein 8; A8), in modulating circulating levels of ApoB (apolipoprotein B)–containing lipoproteins remain poorly defined. Clarifying these relationships will inform next-generation A3-directed therapies. We performed liver perfusion studies to directly compare the number and composition of very-low-density lipoprotein particles secreted from mice with and without A3. To amplify effects on cholesterol metabolism, we generated Ldlr −/− mice expressing wild-type A3, full-length A3, or N-terminal A3 fragments, with or without coexpression of A8, and analyzed plasma lipids, circulating A3 and A8 complexes, and intravascular lipase activities. Complementary in vitro assays and structural modeling were used to assess relative endothelial lipase inhibition by A3 alone or in complex with A8. Liver perfusion studies revealed that A3 inactivation does not alter the rates of hepatic secretion of very-low-density lipoprotein in wild-type or Ldlr −/− mice. Inactivation of A8 alone lowered plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels by ≈20%, an effect dependent upon the expression of both endothelial lipase and A3. Maximal inhibition of lipoprotein lipase required coexpression of A8 plus both full-length A3 and N-terminal A3 fragments, indicating that A3 cleavage, in addition to A8 expression, is essential for maximal lipoprotein lipase inhibition. In contrast, A8 expression, but not A3 cleavage, was required for optimal endothelial lipase inhibition. A8 acts in concert with A3 to differentially modulate lipoprotein lipase– and endothelial lipase–mediated lipolysis, which antagonizes hepatic clearance of newly secreted atherogenic ApoB–containing lipoproteins. This mechanistic framework refines our understanding of A3-targeted lipid lowering and highlights the therapeutic potential of dual A3- plus A8-directed strategies to treat dyslipidemia and prevent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
neb77c6ade6a7: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

n610f679f14c5: Health professionals and policy makers should fully support the students currently protesting in France.1 Apart from the regrettable outbursts of violence happening during protests, this movement reflects the anger of youth at decades of successive policies, both at national and global levels, which have progressively widened educational inequalities. n1d8ac6a16ca9: Degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM), the most common non-traumatic spinal cord injury, is a prevalent, progressive, and highly disabling neurological disease, causing heterogeneous impairment ranging from sensory loss and impaired hand dexterity to gait, balance, and autonomic dysfunction. Disability often persists despite surgical decompression, and untreated disease can progress to irreversible neurological injury, including tetraplegia. Current clinical management is largely reactive, with diagnosis and intervention typically only after neurological deterioration has become clinically apparent and radiographic evidence of cervical myelopathy is established. Advances in multimodal diagnostics over the past 5 years are now enabling the detection of subtle spinal cord injury, biological disease activity, and subclinical neurodegeneration before overt clinical disability. Quantitative spinal cord MRI, advanced neurophysiological assessments, dynamic biomechanical metrics, and sensitive functional testing provide complementary tools for early detection, risk stratification, and prognostication. Together, these approaches are redefining DCM as a disease that should be managed proactively. Evidence supports decompressive surgery in patients with moderate-to-severe disease, whereas in milder disease or in spinal stenosis that might develop into DCM, the management of patients should be interdisciplinary, with active surveillance to detect early deterioration or decompressive surgery in selected cases. Improved prediction of disease trajectories and clearer evidence on long-term outcomes could enable selective earlier intervention and help to prevent neurological disability.
nc01b65fdc7df: Delirium is a common, acute confusional state that is associated with adverse patient, caregiver, and health system outcomes. All patients are at risk for delirium, although those with advanced age or acute infection and those taking sedatives and anticholinergics are at greater risk. The pathophysiology of delirium is complex and includes neuronal injury, inflammation, metabolic imbalance, and blood-brain barrier disruption. It is important to note that delirium is preventable; recognizing people at risk and identifying and addressing predisposing and precipitating factors is paramount. No single intervention or medication has been shown to be effective in treating delirium; therefore, standard-of-care treatments rely on multifaceted strategies to address contributing factors.
nfbbb69d4eccb: Cervical cancer is the third most common gynecologic cancer, with more than 13 000 new cases diagnosed in 2025. The incidence of and mortality from cervical cancer vary across racial and ethnic groups and in persons living in medically underserved or geographically isolated areas, with half of all cervical cancers occurring in women who are underscreened or have never been screened. Persistent infection with high-risk types of human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most important risk factor for cervical cancer and is associated with nearly all cases. Although genital tract HPV infection is common, most HPV infections are transient, and cervical cancer occurs in only a small portion of patients with HPV. For decades, cervical cancer screening relied on annual cytologic assessment. A growing understanding of the role of HPV infection in the natural progression of cervical cancer has led to updated screening recommendations from the American Cancer Society and the Women's Preventive Services Initiative, as well as a draft update from the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force. These recommendations include primary HPV testing as a preferred screening strategy and include an option for self-collected specimens for HPV testing. Here, 2 experts in this field, a primary care physician and an obstetrics and gynecology physician, debate how to apply these guidelines when screening a patient for cervical cancer. They discuss a range of screening options and consider the challenges of applying these guidelines across different age groups and in patients at increased risk.
nd1eb029ace1c: Chronic liver disease is an increasingly prevalent and heterogeneous syndrome with important consequences for cardiovascular function. As the global burdens of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis continue to rise, cardiovascular disease has emerged as a major driver of overall morbidity and mortality in affected patients. Despite the growing recognition of the intersectionality between hepatology and cardiology care clinically, cardiovascular disease risk among patients with liver disease is underrecognized. This state-of-the-art review summarizes the current understanding of the bidirectional interactions between the liver and the cardiovascular system. Shared mechanisms—including inflammation, endothelial injury, and neurohormonal overactivation—that contribute to the development of adverse myocardial remodeling, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, arrhythmias, pulmonary vascular syndromes, and cirrhosis-associated cardiovascular syndromes are reviewed. A specific focus is placed on metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease, the most common form of chronic liver disease, while highlighting the distinct cardiovascular manifestations associated with other types of chronic liver disease. These include alcohol-associated liver disease and infiltrative diseases that affect the liver and heart with cardiovascular implications across the spectrum from early stages of liver disease through cirrhosis. We discuss practical approaches to detecting liver disease, including the assessment of liver fibrosis noninvasively in individuals at risk. We discuss the approach to assessing cardiovascular risk through cardiac imaging, biomarkers, and cardiac functional testing once chronic liver disease is detected. Management considerations for commonly encountered cardiovascular conditions and a critical appraisal of the evolving evidence supporting cardiometabolic therapies in patients with chronic liver disease are discussed to underscore potential cardiovascular and liver benefits. Critical evidence gaps and future research priorities are identified, including the development and evaluation of liver-informed cardiovascular risk models, incorporation of cardiovascular end points into liver disease trials, and implementation of integrated cardiohepatometabolic care pathways. Improved recognition of chronic liver disease and related cardiovascular disease risk represents a major opportunity to facilitate earlier disease detection, enhance risk stratification, and improve outcomes across the spectrum of chronic liver disease.
n2adff0cef0e3: The UK (chiefly driven by England and Scotland) is expected to be the first country to meet WHO's goal for the elimination of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection by 2030. In April, 2026, the UK Health Security Agency's analysis of progress by the National Health Service (NHS) towards elimination showed that 84·6% of people living with HCV had been diagnosed and prevalence in people who inject drugs had fallen to 5·2% in 2024, with an estimated incidence of 4·4 infections per 100 person-years, predicted to fall below WHO's target of two infections per 100 patient-years by 2030.
n22a7e8b53682: In many disease settings, physicians and patients can choose between several treatment options that are in common use, but how should they make the choice? The problem is often not the absence of evidence but the absence of robust randomised controlled evidence directly comparing treatments that are already widely used in practice. Treatment options might have been directly compared with a common comparator, but not to each other; for example, in respiratory syncytial virus prevention in infants, both maternal vaccination and infant monoclonal antibodies have shown efficacy versus placebo but have not been directly compared.
nc15a259c1b66: Left atrial (LA) stiffening augments the LA V wave, pressurizing the pulmonary artery (PA) out of proportion to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure. We characterized the pathophysiologic, diagnostic, and clinical implications of LA stiffening, as defined by prominent V waves, in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. In this retrospective cohort study, patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and less than moderate mitral regurgitation at rest underwent invasive hemodynamic exercise testing. Patients with heightened operant LA stiffening were defined by the PA wedge pressure (PAWP) V wave exceeding mean PAWP by ≥10 mm Hg. A previously used formula for V wave–corrected PAWP was validated against the PAWP waveform pressure-time-area to explore impact of the V wave on transpulmonary pressure gradients. Clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and outcome data were compared for patients with and without prominent V waves. Compared with patients without prominent V waves (n=844, 79%), those with prominent V waves (n=225, 21%) were older and more likely to be women, with more severe LA myopathy, evidenced by greater LA volume index (42.2±15.0 versus 32.5±13.0 mL/m 2 , P <0.001), lower LA reservoir strain (16.4±7.5% versus 23.2±8.3%, P <0.001), more atrial fibrillation (61.3% versus 22.9%, P <0.001), and increased operant LA reservoir stiffness (0.59±0.25 versus 0.23±0.24 mm Hg/mL, P <0.001). Patients with prominent V waves had markedly higher PA systolic pressure than those without (54±16 versus 38±12 mm Hg, P <0.001) despite no difference in end-diastolic PAWP-PA pressure gradient (3±5 versus 3±4 mm Hg, P =0.950). Incorporating the V wave into PAWP improved correlation between directly measured PAWP pressure-time integral compared with mid–A wave PAWP (R 2 =0.96 versus R 2 =0.86, P <0.001 for comparison). In patients with prominent V waves, the prevalence of combined pre- and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension decreased from 60.2% to 29.3% after V wave correction for the transpulmonary pressure gradients. Despite similar corrected pulmonary vascular resistances in patients with and without prominent V waves, apparent PA compliance was much lower in patients with prominent V waves (3.03±1.56 versus 4.90±2.27 mL/mm Hg, P <0.001), augmenting right ventricular afterload, and these changes were coupled with more severe right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, blunted cardiopulmonary exercise reserve, and increased risk of hospitalization for heart failure or death in patients with versus without prominent V waves (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53–2.86]; P <0.001). More than 1 in 5 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction display prominent V waves in excess of end-diastolic PAWP. This augments right ventricular afterload due to backward transmission of the V wave, contributing to right heart failure that is independent of the pulmonary vasculature. Failure to account for the V wave during hemodynamic assessment overestimates the severity of pulmonary vascular disease present.
n94a9e0fcb5d2: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. And understandably so. Important progress has been made through often courageous direct action. But this sharply competitive approach is, according to a new Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health, dangerously flawed. Indeed, perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms.
nb8510b0ee181: By 2050, almost 1 billion people are expected to live with osteoarthritis—a disabling musculoskeletal condition with currently no cure. Despite its burden and costs, osteoarthritis remains largely invisible in national and global health agendas, is poorly integrated within service models for other chronic health conditions, and is frequently perceived as inevitable with ageing and associated with limited therapeutic options. This context drives an osteoarthritis identity problem that fuels frustration among those living with the disease and health-care professionals, perpetuates stigma and inequities, undermines access to effective interventions, and crucially, deprioritises osteoarthritis in health policy.
n8c924c41350f: The Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health's report by Christopher J L Murray and colleagues uses forecasts based on expected cumulative amenable disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) to quantify and compare threats from 2025 to 2100.1 The Commission's intent is to equip governments with the tools to make smart long-term decisions that reduce risk based on “systematic, repeatable risk assessment and preparedness planning” as opposed to “short-termism and localism”.

n52a03cc987e2: “I’m concerned that the narrative now around ageing populations is one of doom and gloom. But long-lived populations are not the problem. The problem is that we haven’t allowed people to get to an older age healthy”, says John Wong, Executive Director of the Centre for Population Health at the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Executive Director of The Yong Pung How and Yong Wei-Woo Centre at the National University Health System (NUHS), Singapore. “Two-thirds of the world is now below the fertility replacement rate, and unless we keep our populations healthy throughout their whole lifespan, we’ll have this major challenge of more and more unwell older people”, continued Wong, who is also Isabel Chan Professor in Medical Sciences in the Division of Haematology-Oncology at the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, NUS, and Emeritus Consultant in the Department of Haematology-Oncology, National University Cancer Institute, NUHS, Singapore.
n3c52f9a5e96d: Our decisions today can support or threaten future human health. Insofar as we protect the planet or invest in fruitful research on pandemic countermeasures, we promote future wellbeing and health, sometimes at the present generation's expense. As we warm the planet, accelerate antibiotic resistance, or consume finite natural resources, we might serve present-day wellbeing or health at the expense of future generations. To decide which such trade-offs are legitimate or advisable, we need to know how to balance the health interests of future generations against each other and against our own.
n9ace97f52042: This report from the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health lays out a foresight-driven, health-focused approach to identifying and prioritising major threats to global health over the remainder of the century. We argue that recent global shocks (including COVID-19, Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease, major geopolitical conflict, accelerating climate impacts, rapid shifts in development assistance, and the emergence of powerful artificial intelligence [AI] systems) show how quickly assumptions about stability can be overturned—and why governments and multilateral institutions must counter short-termism and localism with systematic, repeatable risk assessment and preparedness planning.
n3236834c743b: BackgroundDespite high invasive breast cancer detection rates, the effectiveness of digital breast tomosynthesis screening is still uncertain. We aimed to compare the invasive interval cancer rates in women screened with digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised two-dimensional (s2D) mammography with those screened with digital mammography.MethodsTOSYMA is a multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised, controlled, superiority trial done at 17 screening sites across two federal states in Germany. Women aged 50-70 years were randomly allocated (1:1) to digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography or digital mammography. The first primary endpoint of TOSYMA (TOSYMA-1) was the detection rate of invasive breast cancer and has been previously reported. The second primary endpoint (TOSYMA-2) was the invasive interval cancer rate, defined as the proportion of women who developed an invasive breast cancer in the 24-month interval after being negative at screening (ie, no ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive breast cancer detection) in TOSYMA-1. The primary endpoint was analysed in all participants with a negative screening result in TOSYMA-1. The cumulative incidence of invasive interval cancers at 12 months in screen-negative women was the prespecified secondary outcome. Suspected interval cancers were identified by data linkage to cancer registries. The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03377036) and is closed to accrual but follow-up is ongoing.FindingsBetween July 5, 2018, and Dec 30, 2020, 99 689 women were enrolled in TOSYMA-1 and 99 558 participants included in the modified full analysis set of TOSYMA-1. The median age was 57 years (IQR 53-62) in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set and all participants were female. 49 299 (99·1%) of 49 762 women assigned digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screened negative in TOSYMA-1, as were 49 456 (99·3%) of 49 796 women assigned digital mammography who had evaluable data and were included in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set. Invasive interval cancers were detected in 70 of 49 299 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (invasive interval rate 14·2 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 92 of 49 456 women in the digital mammography group (18·6 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0·76 [95% CI 0·55-1·06]; p=0·11). Invasive interval cancers were detected within 12 months in 22 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (4·5 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 31 women in the digital mammography group (6·3 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; OR 0·71 [95% CI 0·52-0·97]).InterpretationTOSYMA-2 indicates that about a quarter of invasive interval cancers occurring with digital mammography over 2 years might be avoided with digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screening. Although the primary outcome of TOSYMA-2 did not reach statistical significance, this large, randomised trial adds substantial evidence to the use of digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography in breast cancer screening.FundingDeutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (German Research Foundation).

na8a6a0e1f507: Oral deucrictibant provided faster times to symptom relief than placebo and was generally well tolerated. n2a9b380c93d0: Patients increasingly use conversational artificial intelligence (AI), including for possible diagnoses, before seeing a clinician. However, clinical evidence is lacking and is mostly synthetic. The Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer (AMIE), for example, outperformed primary care physicians in text consultations, but its patients were patient actors.1 One exception is a randomised trial of 2069 patients in which a chatbot generated histories, preliminary diagnoses, and test orders, sometimes without staff support, although its primary outcomes focused mainly on efficiency.
n2376de425ee2: Hereditary angioedema due to a deficiency of C1 inhibitor (HAE-C1INH) is clinically characterised by recurrent, generally unpredictable attacks of angioedema.1 Untreated episodes are often severe and prolonged, lasting up to 3–5 days and engendering considerable morbidity and even mortality.2 Unlike angioedema associated with mast cell mediators, the swelling in HAE-C1INH does not respond to antihistamines, corticosteroids, or epinephrine.
n6110c6569e80: On May 15, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda declared outbreaks of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus. On May 17, 2026, the Director-General of WHO determined that the epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, approximately 48 h after the outbreak declarations.1 By Aug 26, 2026, 5815 confirmed cases and 2788 deaths had been reported, including 5794 cases and 2786 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where transmission had spread to 60 health zones across six provinces.
n95dba68dac5b: Migraine is a chronic neurovascular disorder characterised by recurrent attacks of moderate-to-severe head pain, accompanied by transient but disabling symptoms such as aura, nausea, vomiting, phonophobia, and photophobia, reflecting the involvement of multiple systems. Migraine affects and disables a large proportion of the global population. The pathogenesis of migraine involves the interplay of genetic and epigenetic factors across complex neurosensory and neurovascular networks. Decades of research have elucidated key components of these pathways, driving the development of mechanism-based therapies that are now transforming clinical practice and substantially improving patients’ lives.
ncdd2549a8145: BackgroundNeoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery is standard treatment for advanced ovarian cancer that is unlikely to achieve optimal cytoreduction. We aimed to evaluate a chemotherapy-free regimen of neoadjuvant niraparib monotherapy in homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)-positive disease initially unsuitable for primary debulking surgery.MethodsThis single-arm, phase 2 trial was conducted at six tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, had treatment-naïve, FIGO stage III-IV HRD-positive high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian cancer, an ECOG performance status of 0-2, with a low likelihood of complete primary debulking surgery based on prespecified criteria. Patients received oral niraparib monotherapy for two 28-day cycles with an individualised starting dose of 200 mg or 300 mg. Protocol-permitted supportive care was provided as clinically indicated. Co-primary endpoints were investigator-assessed objective response rate in the response-evaluable population and R0 resection rate after interval debulking surgery in the operated population. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of niraparib. The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04507841), is closed to enrolment, and this report presents the primary analysis.FindingsBetween Jan 8, 2021, and Jul 18, 2023, 127 patients were screened, and 67 were enrolled into the study. All enrolled patients were female and self-identified as Han Chinese (median age 55 years [IQR 50-62]). At the data cutoff (Dec 29, 2025), median follow-up was 37·7 months (IQR 31·8-48·5). Among 48 response-evaluable patients, 30 achieved an objective response, with an objective response rate of 63% (95% CI 47-76). Among 40 operated patients, 32 achieved R0 resection, with an R0 resection rate of 80% (95% CI 64-91). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were thrombocytopenia in 32 (48%) of 67 patients, leukopenia in 13 (19%) patients, anaemia in 12 (18%) patients, and neutropenia in nine (13%) patients. Serious adverse events occurred in 19 (28%) patients. No treatment-related deaths occurred.InterpretationNeoadjuvant niraparib showed anti-tumour activity and enabled R0 resection in selected patients with HRD-positive advanced ovarian cancer who were initially unsuitable for primary debulking surgery. This strategy remains investigational and requires randomised validation against standard platinum-taxane neoadjuvant chemotherapy.FundingNational Key Technology Research and Development Program of China, National Natural Science Foundation of China, Natural Science Foundation of Hubei Province, Innovative Drug Research and Development National Science and Technology Major Project, and Zai Lab (Shanghai).TranslationFor the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.
n38c614a80e8a: BackgroundPostacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (long COVID) presents a therapeutic challenge, with fatigue being a common, debilitating symptom.ObjectiveTo assess the efficacy of fluvoxamine and metformin to treat long COVID fatigue.DesignRandomized, placebo-controlled, adaptive trial. n3b8cc50245aa: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) is an acute event associated with high mortality. Although survival has improved in high-income countries, contemporary multicenter data from low- and middle-income countries remain scarce, limiting global benchmarking and the identification of system-level opportunities for improvement. This cohort study used data from the BASIC-IHCA (Baseline Investigation of In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest) registry. Adult patients (≥18 years) who experienced IHCA and received cardiopulmonary resuscitation between July 1, 2019, and December 31, 2020, at 37 hospitals across 29 provinces in China were included. The primary outcome was survival to 30 days or hospital discharge. Secondary outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation, 6- and 12-month survival, and favorable neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score 1–2). Process measures focused on the timeliness of resuscitation response and the implementation of postresuscitation interventions. Among 17 602 patients (median age, 66 years; 65.5% male), the annual incidence of adult IHCA was 4.1 per 1000 admissions. Cardiac etiology was identified in 6569 (37.3%) patients, and 2380 (13.5%) presented with initial shockable rhythm. Among all patients, 16 872 (95.9%) received cardiopulmonary resuscitation within 1 minute; timely defibrillation or epinephrine was achieved in 71.4% and 84.4% of patients with initial shockable and nonshockable rhythms, respectively. Sustained return of spontaneous circulation was achieved in 6200 (35.2%) patients, of whom 222 (3.6%) received temperature control therapy and 320 (5.2%) underwent coronary angiography. Overall, 1610 (9.1%) patients survived to 30 days or discharge, with 1241 (7.1%) having a favorable neurological outcome. At 12 months, 1075 (6.1%) patients remained alive, and 986 (5.6%) had a favorable neurological outcome. This multicenter registry highlights a substantial burden of IHCA in China, with markedly low survival rates. Despite prompt initial resuscitation, critical gaps persist in postresuscitation care. Systemic and cultural factors, including the infrequent use of do not attempt cardiopulmonary resuscitation orders, may further contribute to survival disparities. These findings suggest several system-level opportunities to improve IHCA outcomes, including structured response systems, optimized critical care resource allocation, and greater integration of advanced care planning.
n219f8a408bdb: Digital technologies are transforming societal structures, but this transformation and its public health impacts occur unevenly across the global population.1 In a new Lancet Series about the digital determinants of health (DDoH), the authors propose a coordinated and systemic approach for examining and responding to the challenges that digitalisation presents for global health and wellbeing.2–4 Social media use by young people emerges in the Series as an important starting point for examining the DDoH.
nef6b4c0cb55a: Few who remember the idealistic vision of the 1990s World Wide Web could have anticipated the extent to which the internet would reshape modern life. Today's children have never lived in a world without smartphones and ubiquitous digital connectivity, and must contend with online shaming and bullying, permanent digital footprints, and weaponised attention economies. Generative artificial intelligence can now detach us from reality, providing emotional support and companionship for some, while supplying our most personal disclosures to trillion-dollar tech companies.
n6932b5bcbf13: The psychoanalyst and paediatrician Donald Winnicott proposed that a child discovers his or her own self through creative play. This certainly seems to be the case for Barbara Prainsack, Professor for Comparative Policy Analysis and Director of the Centre for the Study of Contemporary Solidarity at the University of Vienna, Austria. “I remember that when I was a young kid,” she says, “I played with little figurines—Playmobil—and I wrote their constitution.” It seems her interest in “how society works and what holds it together” was an innate quality during those early years.
nacc14a77a206: The digital determinants of health are the structural conditions through which digital infrastructures, business models, and design choices shape health outcomes. Yet these determinants remain largely outside public health policy and remain fragmented across regulatory sectors. Rather than regulating individual technologies in isolation, governance should ensure that digital systems and environments advance population health and reduce inequities. A public health approach shifts attention from individual responsibility—and the tendency to blame users—towards the governance of the structural features that produce health risks and inequities.
nb813cbb099e2: Digital transformations exert increasing influence over the lives of the global population, shaping opportunities and generating harms for health and wellbeing across the spectrum of digital access and engagement. The scale of influence of digital transformations on human and planetary health marks the urgency of attention to the digital determinants of health (DDoH). In this Series paper, we describe a prevailing digital sociotechnological order (DSTO) as the structural source of the DDoH. The DSTO is composed of a set of dominant assumptions that motivate digital practices operating through four features (political norms, economic logics, infrastructures, and personal and social practices) to affect human and planetary health.
n7f09d0415580: Children and adolescents are growing up in a hybrid world in which digital media has become part of the infrastructure of everyday life and a structural determinant of their health. In the second paper of this Series on the digital determinants of health, we apply the framework introduced in the first paper to one of the most contested questions in public health: how young people's digital media use shapes their health and wellbeing. Using the digital determinants of health framework to interpret the current evidence base, we examine what is known, and what remains poorly understood, about the public health implications of children's and adolescents’ digital media use.

n162e3d5f7ec8: In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. n4e31fa871866: Treatment with retatrutide resulted in substantial improvements in bodyweight and was associated with improvements in glycaemic control in participants with obesity and type 2 diabetes, with a safety profile generally consistent with other molecules with GLP-1 receptor agonism. nc683da59c2a8: In this Clinical Rounds, we present a case of neuroborreliosis in a man aged 59 years who initially complained of headache, tremor, and hiccups. Diagnosis was delayed, partly due to an atypical presentation but mainly because subtle MRI findings were overlooked. n2a9009ad8e49: Climate change is shaping health in the 21st century. In the past few weeks alone, Nepal has faced unprecedented flash floods, and multiple countries have experienced deadly heatwaves and catastrophic wildfires.1 El Niño is now firmly established and projected to intensify further.2 The southern hemisphere faces a summer of extreme heatwaves, droughts, and floods, threatening maternal and child health in particular, and increasing infectious disease outbreaks.3 Populations in lower-income countries bear a disproportionate burden of these impacts, but are least responsible for emissions and have few resources to respond.
n66f772633bae: The goal of adjuvant systemic therapy after locoregional treatment of cancer is to increase the probability of cure by eradicating micro-metastases. Adjuvant treatment adds side-effects and can impair health-related quality of life (HRQOL); this must be balanced against a reduction in the probability of recurrence, which has a substantial negative effect on HRQOL. Since many adjuvant therapies lead to small gains in relapse-free or overall survival, the severity and duration of treatment-related side-effects and their impact on patient functioning and overall HRQOL are relevant to clinical decision making. To facilitate understanding by oncologists and patients, we recommend reporting in publications the proportion of patients receiving adjuvant therapy who experience a prespecified deterioration in a relevant and validated HRQOL scale, and the duration of this deterioration during and after treatment completion, with appropriate handling of missing data and intercurrent events. HRQOL assessment should include symptoms, functioning domains, and overall HRQOL. Between-group comparisons should address key HRQOL outcomes (as defined by both oncologists and patients) supplemented by descriptive outcomes across remaining HRQOL domains. Once the proportion of patients with specific adverse changes in symptoms is identified, it is possible to determine if specific patient group(s) are at particular risk for these effects. HRQOL information should be included in the primary report of trials evaluating adjuvant therapy as it is key to informed decisions about treatment choice, and updated long-term evaluation is also important to capture any lasting deficits in HRQOL.
n4ad77fd1f706: Garetosmab substantially reduced the number of new heterotopic bone lesions, providing robust evidence of its potential to be an efficacious and generally well tolerated disease-modifying therapy for FOP.
nb1b8b80f345b: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is among the most devastating musculoskeletal disorders. FOP is caused by activating variants in ACVR1, most often arising de novo, and is characterised by congenital malformations of the great toes, followed by episodic flare-ups and progressive heterotopic ossification in soft tissues.1,2 Lesions can be triggered by minor trauma, intramuscular injections, or surgery, but can also arise without an identifiable trigger. Over time, heterotopic bone forms a second skeleton, progressively restricting movement of the jaw, spine, hips, shoulders, and thorax.
nc5d5b61056f6: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognised as a clinically modifiable determinant of efficacy and toxicity across systemic cancer therapies, with the most mature evidence in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). The composition and function of intestinal microbes can influence treatment outcomes by affecting immune priming, antigen presentation, host-microbial co-metabolism, drug biotransformation, and epithelial barrier integrity. In melanoma, non-small-cell lung cancer, and renal cell carcinoma, higher microbial diversity, ecological stability, and enrichment of immunostimulatory pathways have been associated with improved ICI response and survival. By contrast, antibiotics and proton pump inhibitors are linked to inferior outcomes because they disrupt the microbiome. Microbiome-directed interventions, including faecal microbiota transplantation, dietary modifications, prebiotics, probiotics, and live biotherapeutic products, are undergoing clinical testing but remain at the investigational stage. This Review synthesises current evidence linking the intestinal microbiome to anticancer therapy outcomes, evaluates strategies and challenges for therapeutic modulation of the microbiome, and introduces emerging insights into the mycobiome.
na678dbd0b502: BackgroundInfectious agents are an important preventable cause of cancer globally.
